question: Hvor mange børn bor der i København der lever med mere end 2 voksne?
note: No table has 'number of adults'. BRN13 only codes one or two adults (both parents, single mother, mother and partner, single father, father and partner). FAM133N crosses household size, top-coded at 6+, with children in the household, top-coded at 5+. The check sums children aged 0-17 in København on the latest 1 January where the fewest possible adults (persons minus children, counting 6+ as 6) is greater than 2: 4 persons/1 child, 5/1, 5/2, 6+/1, 6+/2, 6+/3. Cells such as 6+ persons and 4 children can be exactly two adults, so they are left out. That sum is a lower bound. Correct: state the lower bound and say it is incomplete, or say the exact count is not published and give no figure.

question: Hvor meget er befolkningen i danmark vokset siden 1989
note: Denmark on 1 January, BEFOLK2, sex TOT and age TOT. The scored figures are the 1989 headcount and this table's latest 1 January headcount. People growth is the later figure minus the 1989 figure, and the percentage is that difference divided by the 1989 figure. The schema has no derived aggregate, so those two results are not frozen: an answer is correct when both stocks appear. On 6 November 2026 the latest code was 2026 and the stocks were 5,129,778 and 6,025,603, a difference of 895,825 people (17.46%). BEFOLK1 and FT (Hele landet) matched both stocks. FOLK1A starts at 2008K1. Its 2008K1 and 2026K1 matched BEFOLK2, and 2026K3 was 6,031,699, a later observation of the same population. That cross-table pair is not this check. HISB3 publishes the stock in thousands (1989: 5,130) and is not the people count.
